page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 series. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The processor features an extensive cache configuration, including 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), along with hardware cryptography engines (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Memory capacity is fixed at 64.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational efficiency in CPU-intensive operations and data transformation workloads. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores rank in the top 25% at 2190.0 and 17408.0, respectively, backed by top-tier text processing performance (2901.0, top 10%). Compression benchmarks highlight fast execution, with gzip single-threaded compression reaching 35.73 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 204.86 GB/sec (both top 25%). Memory throughput is solid, recording 154.42 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 62.53 GB/sec for uncached writes across large 256 MB blocks. Thanks to AVX-512 and AMX instructions, lightweight CPU-based language model inference shows notable capability, reaching 362.36 tokens/sec on 135M model text generation (top 10%) and 185.31 tokens/sec on 7B model prompt processing.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio yields a lean hardware footprint optimized for pure computation rather than memory-heavy datasets. The omission of local scratch storage necessitates dependency on remote block storage, introducing remote I/O latency considerations for write-heavy workloads. This instance profile offers high resource efficiency for environments that require dense compute threads, fast cryptographic operations, compression pipelines, CI/CD compilation, and static web serving, while memory-intensive databases and high-parameter neural network training are outside its intended operational envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v7 is an x86_64 instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz with a 480 MB L3 cache. Configured with 64.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), this machine has a reduced memory-to-core ratio suited for compute-focused applications. The platform supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets, which assist in strong compression speeds, including 204.86 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and efficient lightweight LLM inference. The instance includes neither integrated GPUs nor local disk storage, necessitating network storage attachments. With strong single-thread and multi-thread Geekbench scores, D32ls_v7 delivers high compute efficiency for compile jobs, compression pipelines, static web serving, and microservices requiring raw CPU throughput without extensive memory footprint.
